{{Short description|Norwegian mathematician (1935–2020)}}
[[File:Helge Tverberg.jpg|thumb|220px|Helge Tverberg at [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 1981]]
'''Helge Arnulf Tverberg''' (March 6, 1935{{snd}}December 28, 2020) was a [[Norwegian people|Norwegian]] [[mathematician]]. He was a professor in the Mathematics Department at the [[University of Bergen]], his speciality being [[combinatorics]]; he retired at the mandatory age of seventy.

He was born in [[Bergen]].<ref>{{citation |title=Meet the mathematician, Helge Tverberg |date=November 22, 2001 |url=http://meldinger.uib.no/engelsk.php?id=191101115828 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611004034/http://meldinger.uib.no/engelsk.php?id=191101115828 |publisher=University of Bergen |archive-date=2015-06-11}}</ref> He took the [[cand.real.]] degree at the University of Bergen in 1958, and the [[dr.philos.]] degree in 1968. He was a lecturer from 1958 to 1971 and professor from 1971 to his retirement in 2005. He was a visiting scholar at the [[University of Reading]] in 1966 and at the [[Australian National University]], in Canberra, from 1980 to 1981, 1987 to 1988 and in 2004.<ref>{{cite news|title=70 år 6. mars: Professor, dr. philos. Helge Arnulf Tverberg|agency=Norwegian News Agency|date=23 February 2005|language=Norwegian}}</ref> He was a member of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27624|title=Gruppe 1: Matematiske fag|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]|language=Norwegian|accessdate=29 October 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927170150/http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27624|archive-date=27 September 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Tverberg, in 1965, proved a result on intersection patterns of partitions of [[point configuration]]s that has come to be known  as [[Tverberg's partition theorem]]. It inaugurated a new branch of [[combinatorial geometry]], with many variations and applications. An account by [[Günter M. Ziegler]] of Tverberg's work in this direction appeared in the issue of the Notices of the American Mathematical Society for April, 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201104/rtx110400550p.pdf|title=3N Colored Points in a Plane}}</ref>
